Targets may be uiapp|uidoc|doc|view or $priorId; arguments may reference a prior result as {$ref:'priorId'}. Body: {operations:[{id,op:construct|call|get_property,memberId?,property?,target?,args?:[]}],returns?:[$id],maxTotalMs?:250..10000,maxOperationMs?:100..10000}. V2 remains read-only and rejects mutating, freeze-risk, and non-low-risk members. The exact SDK Element.GetDependentElements read is graph-only with args:[null]; no filter deserialization. Returned collections carry complete/truncated/hasMore flags; a truncated collection is not a complete dependency census.

candidates.title: Native API Transaction Operations
candidates.description: Execute up to 16 reflected operations inside one explicit Revit transaction. Supports generic 3D placeholder solids: construct lines/arcs, CurveLoop.Create, CreateExtrusionGeometry, then DirectShape.CreateElement and SetShape. Use graph_allowed member ids and typed prior-result arguments {$ref:'id'}, including collection arguments such as [[{$ref:'curve_a'},{$ref:'curve_b'}]]; target:$id selects an instance. References exist only within this request. Supported detached geometry is bounded to the documented factories and Curve/CurveLoop/Solid/GeometryObject references, not arbitrary objects or ShapeBuilder. Nested collections are bounded; see the generic one-foot placeholder example. This high-risk route requires a write grant, at least one persisted model mutation, active-document ownership, a 1..64 affected-element cap, and explicit commit or rollback. Choose commit for authorized application; rollback is optional preview or an explicit user request. A generic solid has no MEP connectors or inferred service. At the real transaction boundary, a document-scoped Dynamic Model Updater observes affected ids and failure processing verifies the in-scope commit or rollback. Body: {operations:[{id,op:construct|call|get_property,memberId?,property?,target?,args?:[]}],returns?:[$id],transaction:{mode:rollback|commit,name?,maxAffectedElements,allowCreate?,allowedExistingElementIds?:[]},maxTotalMs?:250..10000,maxOperationMs?:100..10000}.

candidates.title: Find Elements by Category
candidates.description: This route searches the active host document. For linked inventory independent of view visibility, use POST /revit/quantify with scope=links or both and exact categories. Inspect sourceCoverage: it covers direct source-document instances, not room membership or hidden/nested completeness. Discover existing host Rooms and Spaces by category, name and level before choosing a RoomTag or SpaceTag. Omit viewId and sheetNumber for document-wide discovery: spatial elements hidden in a view are absent from its visible inventory, so that absence does not prove the host lacks a corresponding room or space. Match exact identity, level and placement before using a host space for an annotation of a linked room. Count placed elements by category and group returned family and type only when itemsComplete is true. A truncated result is not a complete inventory. Selector helper: find element ids by scope (viewId OR sheetNumber) and filters. Supports sheet-region targeting, visible-text search, and bounded document discovery across instance name, family, type, category, and Mark. identityTerms uses exact phrase or at-least-half meaningful-token overlap and returns the matched evidence. physicalElementsOnly excludes view-owned/non-model artifacts; topLevelInstancesOnly excludes nested children. expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters performs a second, category-grounded scan for delimiter-bounded phrase acronyms in string parameters and returns the exact parameter evidence; it never expands without a first-pass physical identity seed. includeGeometry adds each physical result's world-space location, axis-aligned bounding box, orientation, type, level, host, and location-curve length/straightness. Agent projections expose routeCurveCandidates for bounded duct/pipe edit discovery; connector topology must still be verified before mutation. Body: {viewId?,sheetNumber?,includeSheetElements?,includeViewportElements?,sheetRegions?:[{minU,minV,maxU,maxV}],regionPaddingFt?,category?,categories?,typeNameContains?,familyNameContains?,nameContains?,markContains?,textContains?,identityTerms?:string[],physicalElementsOnly?,topLevelInstancesOnly?,expandIdentityAcronymsInParameters?,includeGeometry?,limit?}.

candidates.title: Locate Elements
candidates.description: Spatial locator helper for filtering elements by category, level, room, and proximity. It also reports nested-parent evidence. Set spatialResolution=geometry or geometry_with_nearest to batch-resolve each result against host Rooms, host Spaces, and transformed linked architectural Rooms with explicit resolved/ambiguous/unresolved status and provenance. spatialVerticalScope=volume (default) requires strict 3D containment. spatialVerticalScope=same_level requires geometry, ignores native association-only evidence, and uses the target's factual level plus 2D room footprint for above-ceiling/plenum devices; it never searches other levels. If same_level is paired with association, the handler promotes the request to geometry. An explicit phase or active-view phase is strict. When neither exists, the read-only fallback first checks mapped phases where the target exists. If those phases contain no factual room footprint, it may use all mapped phase variants only when the same-level containing variants agree on one numbered spatial identity; phaseFallbackUsed reports that provenance. Unknown mappings, conflicting identities, and boundary-only evidence fail closed. Unavailable link/transform/element-location/level evidence also fails closed. Body: {elementIds?,categories?,levelNames?,roomNumber?,roomNameContains?,nearElementId?,maxDistanceFt?,limit?,spatialResolution?:association|geometry|geometry_with_nearest,spatialVerticalScope?:volume|same_level,spatialKindPreference?:auto|room|space|all,includeHostRooms?,includeHostSpaces?,includeLinkedRooms?,linkedModelNameContains?,phaseId?,phaseName?,nearestCandidateLimit?}.

candidates.title: Create MEP Route
candidates.description: Create a multi-segment duct, pipe, or electrical conduit route from ordered XYZ or frame-linked points with dry-run, conservative size/elevation fallbacks, explicit user-workset assignment, internal connector attempts, optional fail-closed endpoint joining, and native readback. Set requiredExistingEndpoint=start|end|both with exact expectedExistingStartOwnerId/expectedExistingEndOwnerId for required ends; an explicit endpoint takes precedence over requireExistingEndpointConnections, while true alone requires both ends. Duplicate duct/pipe/conduit type names fail closed; use ductTypeId, pipeTypeId, or conduitTypeId for stable native selection. Duct profiles and dimensions must be valid and compatible before starting a transaction. Native route size, duct shape, and requested workset readback must match when verify=true. Use dryRun:false for authorized creation and true for a requested preview. Body: {kind:duct|pipe|conduit,frameId?,points:[{x?,y?,z?,xPx?,yPx?,xyz?}],viewId?,roomNumber?,levelName?,levelId?,worksetName?,worksetId?,systemType?,ductType?,ductTypeId?,ductShape?:round|rectangular|oval,pipeType?,pipeTypeId?,conduitType?,conduitTypeId?,ductSize?,diameter?,pipeSize?,segmentSizes?:string[],sizePolicy?:explicit_required|use_default_with_warning,elevationPolicy?:explicit_required|resolve_context_default,routingMode?:orthogonal|polyline,connectSegments?,connectToExisting?,requireExistingEndpointConnections?,requiredExistingEndpoint?:start|end|both,expectedExistingStartOwnerId?,expectedExistingEndOwnerId?,externalConnectionToleranceFt?,verify?,dryRun?}.

candidates.title: Connect Existing MEP Branch
candidates.description: connectionMode=insert_inline_accessory fits one already-loaded unhosted level-based round HVAC duct accessory into an existing straight duct. It requires kind=duct, expectedModelPath, mainElementId/expectedMainUniqueId, expectedMainStartXyz/expectedMainEndXyz, accessoryTypeId/expectedAccessoryTypeUniqueId, insertionPointXyz and instanceRadiusParameter. Use current native identities and coordinates in model feet. The writable instance radius is derived from the host; actual ports must fit the host diameter. Revit splits the duct while retaining the original ID, connects both accessory ports reciprocally, and preserves far peers, remote geometry/parameters, type data and schedules; unsupported changes roll back. No family loading, pressure-loss design or guessed sizing. dryRun=false applies; omitted dryRun defaults to rollback. After commit use one independent get-connectors read with includeInlineAccessoryState=true, exact physical host/split/accessory/remote IDs, exact preservationScheduleIds from preservationBefore, includeAllRefs/includeCoordinateSystem/includeFlexGeometry=true and maxConnectorsPerElement=512. This read proves fit/preservation, not sheet appearance or saved delivery. Never repeat a committed insertion to verify. Explicit connectionMode=replace_tee_with_takeoff atomically replaces one connected round duct tee with a straight bridge and native takeoff while retaining both old main ducts and the rigid/flex branch. It requires kind=duct, teeElementId, mainElementId, secondMainElementId, branchElementId, expectedTakeoffTypeId and verify=true; optional branchConnectorId/expectedBranchOriginXyz guard exact identity. Workset is inherited from the main. dryRun=true performs the native operation then rolls the entire group back; dryRun=false applies. Dependent annotation deletion, unexpected created/deleted elements, mismatched main data or changed far connections cause rollback. After commit, use the supplied independent get-connectors plan with includeTeeReplacementState=true. elementIds contains only surviving main/secondMain/branch and the new bridge/takeoff; replacementRemovedIds contains the deleted tee and actual parent-bound centerlines, replacementTypeIds the retained type scope, and preservationScheduleIds the regular schedules. The current read must establish absence, reciprocal fitted connections, span and retained parameters/types/system/schedules. Dependent annotations and any unexplained owner still cause rollback. The addition-only graph proof is insufficient; do not repeat the replacement for verification. Connect one retained branch to the interior of an existing rigid main without replacing accepted geometry. connectionMode:takeoff_fitting creates a native takeoff between one exact open rigid/flex duct or pipe connector and its main, accepts an explicit worksetId/worksetName, and otherwise inherits the retained branch user workset with committed readback. connectionMode:air_terminal_on_duct uses Revit's direct air-terminal attachment operation, requires kind:duct plus an exact open air-terminal connector, and produces the native direct terminal-to-duct topology without an adapter curve. Both modes guard the active model and projected interior point, preserve pre-existing physical connections, verify the result after transaction commit, and perform the real operation inside a rollback-verified transaction group during dry-run. Body: {expectedModelPath?,connectionMode?:takeoff_fitting|air_terminal_on_duct,kind:duct|pipe,mainElementId,branchElementId,branchConnectorId?,expectedBranchOriginXyz?,originToleranceFt?,expectedTakeoffTypeId?,expectedTakeoffFamilyName?,expectedTakeoffTypeName?,worksetId?,worksetName?,dryRun?,verify?}.

Composes with hosted/unhosted placement, requires compatible open connector shape/domain/size within tolerance, uses one source connector per target, and rolls back if native AllRefs verification does not prove the requested count. Body: {sourceElementId,targetElementIds:[...],toleranceFt?,sizeToleranceFt?,requiredConnectionCount?,dryRun?,verify?}.

candidates.title: Existing Conditions MEP Draft Workflow
candidates.description: Execute one source-grounded reconstruction stage. The Operator harness normally sends one dependency-ready operation per call, but may send a bounded group of explicitly marked independent high-confidence straight backbones. Each stage runs first with dryRun:true and then once with dryRun:false. Later stages pass hash-ledgered priorActionOutputs so accepted native IDs are never replayed. Each call has its own rollback boundary. Responses echo stageKey and persist created_element_ids, affected_element_ids, and route endpoint IDs; the host ledger binds planned continuation endpoints to those IDs and audits their native connectors before acceptance. In addition to route, family, connection, tag, and circuit creation, the wrapper supports repair-first move, rotate, MEP size/elevation edit, and exact connector repair operations against useful existing elements. Body: {stageKey?,priorActionOutputs?:[{action_key,created_element_ids,affected_element_ids?,route_segment_element_ids?,route_start_element_ids?,route_end_element_ids?,split_main_start_element_ids?,split_main_end_element_ids?}],operations:[{action_key,path,depends_on?,apply_body?,deferred_body?,execution_mode?,provisional_batch_key?,continuation_endpoints?}],dryRun?,verify?,maximumCreatedElements?,targetViewId?,applyTargetViewPhase?,requireAllCreatedElementsVisibleInTargetView?}.
candidates.example: dry-run one repairable existing-conditions stage or bounded provisional backbone batch, apply it once, verify it, and persist created or affected IDs

candidates.title: MEP Route Workflow
candidates.description: One-call duct, pipe, or native conduit route workflow that enforces resolve context -> dry-run -> optional apply -> focused post-change highlight/export. Body mirrors create-mep-route, including stable type IDs, explicit worksetName/worksetId, segmentSizes, and optional fail-closed endpoint joining. Set requiredExistingEndpoint=start|end|both with exact expectedExistingStartOwnerId/expectedExistingEndOwnerId; an explicit endpoint takes precedence over requireExistingEndpointConnections, while true alone requires both ends. Plus {apply?:boolean,visualVerify?:boolean,visualViewId?,imageSize?,focusPaddingFt?}. Visual verification is ready only when every created element is found, collected, unhidden, and has a view-specific bounding box in the requested view; otherwise it returns CreatedElementsNotVisibleInView with diagnostics.

candidates.title: MEP Branch Network Workflow
candidates.description: One-call network workflow for a main duct/pipe route plus multiple branch tee/tap connections. Dry-run plans the main route, branch projections, selected sizes, retained branch anchors, branch-level reducer/transition joint plans, and accessory/damper graph nodes. Apply creates the main route first, then connects each branch to its requested main segment using /revit/connect-mep-branch; duct tap/takeoff, pipe tap/takeoff with an explicit Revit takeoff/tap routing preference, retained two-connector transition/reducer anchors, and duct/pipe split tee use the lower-level verified guards. A branch with existingBranchAnchorElementId must use connectionMode:"tee" and never falls back to an open-main or tap path. Accessory graph apply supports explicit duct/pipe accessory insertions hosted on created main or branch segments when a compatible loaded or workspace-scoped familyPath symbol resolves, plus explicit target-id duct/pipe accessory delete and type_change with compatible loaded types. Body: {kind:duct|pipe,mainPoints:[...],mainSegmentSizes?,branches:[{mainSegmentIndex,connectionMode?:tee|tap,connectionPoint?,points:[...],branchSize?,branchSegmentSizes?:string[],existingBranchAnchorElementId?}],accessories?:[{action:insert|delete|type_change,targetElementId?,targetElementIds?,typeId?,targetTypeName?,familySymbolId?,familyPath?,familyName?,typeName?,mainSegmentIndex?,branchIndex?,branchSegmentIndex?,chainageFt?,point?}],viewId?,roomNumber?,levelName?,systemType?,ductType?,pipeType?,ductSize?,diameter?,pipeSize?,apply?,verify?,visualVerify?}.

candidates.title: Reroute MEP Route Segment
candidates.description: Guarded edit workflow for one straight duct/pipe curve. Discover candidates with /revit/find-elements includeGeometry:true and screen routeCurveCandidates before trial calls. A size-transition host must be at least 1.0 ft long so the transition can remain 0.5 ft from both ends. Current endpoint preservation requires exactly two physical End connectors and no side/tap Curve connectors; skip tapped hosts instead of weakening connection checks. Set operation:"offset" or operation:"size_transition" explicitly whenever size metadata is also supplied; omitted/auto preserves legacy inference. Offset mode derives two split points from host curve chainage or normalized chainage, reports replacement segments, offset points, selected type/system/level/size, and expected elbow fittings; offsetMode:"dogleg45" uses diagonal setback legs instead of perpendicular legs. Size-transition mode derives one transition point, reports upstream/downstream segment points, explicit selected sizes, and expected transition fitting. Apply replaces the host only after required fittings/connectors succeed, reports created segment/fitting ids, connector/system audit, endpointReconnectionPlan when applicable, and optional trace-enabled focused capture. Connected host endpoints are blocked by default; set preserveConnectedEndpoints:true only after dry-run reports a resolvable start/end endpointReconnectionPlan to reconnect the replacement route to original external endpoint connectors. Mutation flags are canonical: preview requires apply:false,dryRun:true; write requires apply:true,dryRun:false; omitted or equal pairs are rejected. Body offset: {operation:offset,kind:duct|pipe,hostElementId,split1ChainageFt?|split1Normalized?,split2ChainageFt?|split2Normalized?,offsetVector:{x,y,z},offsetMode?:orthogonal|dogleg45,doglegAngleDegrees?,preserveConnectedEndpoints?,apply,dryRun,verify?,visualVerify?,visualViewId?,focusPaddingFt?}. Body size-transition: {operation:size_transition,kind:duct|pipe,hostElementId,transitionChainageFt?|transitionNormalized?,upstreamDuctSize?|downstreamDuctSize?|upstreamDiameter?|downstreamDiameter?|upstreamPipeSize?|downstreamPipeSize?,sizePolicy?,preserveConnectedEndpoints?,apply,dryRun,verify?,visualVerify?,visualViewId?,focusPaddingFt?}.

candidates.description: Trace connected MEP elements via connectors starting from an element id. Body: {startElementId, systemName?, inferSystemFromStart?, stopAtBranchFittings?, stopAtTransitions?, maxHops?, excludeElementIds?, stopAtElementIds?, stopAtCategories?, includeDucts?, includePipes?, includeFittings?, includeAccessories?, includeTerminals?, includeEquipment?, includeOtherCategories?, maxElements?, includeSystemAudit?, systemAuditMaxElements?}. Returns connected ids grouped by category and ordered by traversal; includeSystemAudit optionally reports disconnectedIds = systemElementIds - connectedIds for duct and pipe systems.

candidates.title: Get Connectors
candidates.description: Get connector identities, origins, sizes, directions, and optional flex duct/pipe control points and tangents for MEP elements. connectorIdBasis is revit_native_connector_id when the active Revit API exposes a durable connector ID; the enumeration_index_with_origin_guard_required fallback must be paired with the returned origin in repair requests. connectedTo preserves all Revit Connector.AllRefs entries; physicalConnectedTo excludes MEPSystem membership objects so isPhysicallyConnected and physicalConnectionCount can be used for actual topology/open-connector checks. Set onlyOpenPhysicalConnectors=true for a compact exhaustive scan that returns summary counts plus only open physical connector rows. Set includeVerificationParameters=true to read System Classification, Reference Level, Width, Height and Diameter in the same native callback as the full connector graph. This mode requires 1-500 unique positive elementIds, includeAllRefs and includeCoordinateSystem, and forbids open-only filtering. It returns verificationParameters with schema revit-operator.duct-verification-parameters/v1; missing fields remain explicit. Set includeInlineAccessoryState=true for one bounded physical/type/parameter/geometry/schedule observation in the same callback, with 1-5 exact physical elementIds and 0-32 disjoint preservationScheduleIds. Complete references, coordinates and flex geometry are required; incomplete observations remain explicit. Alternatively set includeTeeReplacementState=true with 1-8 exact surviving physical elementIds, 0-12 replacementRemovedIds, 0-16 replacementTypeIds and 0-32 preservationScheduleIds, all disjoint. It returns current native owner/type/geometry/parameter facts, actual removed-ID existence, parent-bound centerlines, system membership and complete schedule state. Set includeNativePlacementState=true for the independent native-interactive insertion scope: exact elementIds (1-5000 physical owners), placementTypeIds (one source type), placementSystemIds (0-50), placementChangedIds (0-1024 actual footprint IDs) and preservationScheduleIds (0-32). Keep all references, coordinates and flex geometry. This returns native owner/type/parameter/connected-system/schedule facts and explicit calculated-flow observations, not a fit or performance verdict. Select only one preservation state; removed/type/schedule IDs are not connector-manager targets. Body: {elementIds:[...], includeInlineAccessoryState?, includeTeeReplacementState?, replacementRemovedIds?, replacementTypeIds?, preservationScheduleIds?, includeVerificationParameters?, includeAllRefs?, includeCoordinateSystem?, includeFlexGeometry?, onlyOpenPhysicalConnectors?, maxConnectorsPerElement?}.
